title: LIVE UPDATES: Undas 2026 (Oct. 31, 2026)
summary: Here are the latest news and features as Filipinos prepare on Saturday, October 31, 2026, for the observance of All Saints' Day on November 1.

blocks.text: PITX: Bicol-bound bus trips continue despite Mayon eruption
Despite Mayon Volcano's eruption on Friday morning, bus trips bound for Bicol from the Parañaque Integrated Terminal Exchange (PITX) remain uninterrupted.

In a "24 Oras" report by Jonathan Andal on Friday, PITX said six out of every 10 buses bound for Bicol were already fully booked. However, walk-in passengers could still be accommodated on ordinary and air-conditioned buses with available seats.
While some Bicol-bound passengers expressed concern over Mayon's eruption, they still pushed through with their trips. Others, meanwhile, were unaware of the volcanic activity.
“Nakakapagalala kasi wala po kaming balita talaga na pumutok pala yung bulkan. Hangga’t mayroon pong bumabyahe, parang tutuloy po kami,” said Daisy Belga, a passenger bound for Albay.
(It's worrying because we had no idea that the volcano had erupted. But as long as buses are still operating, we will push through with our trip.)
“Kinakabahan, pero mostly kasi tagilid naman kami, [sa] Polangui. Medyo gilid man pero abot kami ng ashfall,” added Virgie Magalona, another passenger bound for Albay.
(I'm nervous, but we're somewhat off to the side in Polangui. Even though we're not directly in the affected area, ashfall can still reach us.)
In Andal's report, a bus company said its drivers traveling to Bicol had reported no problems along their routes. However, driver Lito Rodriguez said he would remain cautious.
“Medyo delikado. Magpapa-ano na lang, magpapababa muna ng abo,” Rodriguez said.
(It's somewhat dangerous. I'll just wait for the ash to settle first.)
PITX said buses with online reservation systems were already fully booked, but many buses without online booking options continued to operate even without full passenger loads.
Since October 25, PITX has recorded more than one million passengers.
The terminal's security personnel have also confiscated hundreds of prohibited items, including pointed objects and flammable materials.
Passengers heading to their hometowns brought various types of luggage, with some even traveling with their pets.
PITX said pets are generally allowed on buses with their owners, provided they comply with the requirements.
“Usually ina-allow ng mga buses natin. Dapat po may cage, vaccination card at siyempre diaper po,” PITX Deputy Spokesperson Kolyn Gervacio-Calbasa said.
(Our buses generally allow pets, provided they are in cages and have vaccination cards and diapers.)
Meanwhile, large crowds of passengers have also started gathering at the Five Star bus terminal in Cubao, Quezon City, with some trips bound for Cagayan already fully booked.

Victory Liner has increased the number of trips from Manila to Baguio to 250, up from 150, as it expects passenger volume on the route to double to 10,000 starting October 31. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/VBL, GMA News
Manila Port tightens safety measures for Undas 2026 amid passenger surge
Tighter safety measures are being implemented at the Manila Port amid this year’s exodus for Undas, following a RoRo vessel that listed to its right in Real, Quezon, on Friday morning.
In a "24 Oras report by Ian Cruz on Friday, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) conducted thorough inspections at the port to ensure that cargo on the vessels is properly secured.

“Binigyan na po natin ng instruction ang ating mga inspector na busisiin nang maigi ‘yung mga cargo lalong-lalo na itong mga rolling cargo o mga sasakyan na sakay ng vessel, na siguraduhing nakatali at maayos dahil konting galaw lang po ng barko maaari po ‘yang mag-move at ma-outbalance ang barko pwede po siyang tumagilid,” Coast Guard Station Manila Deputy Commander P/Lt. Luther Quela said.

(We have already instructed our inspectors to meticulously check cargo—especially rolling cargo or vehicles on board the vessel—to ensure they are properly tied down and secured, because even a slight movement of the ship can cause them to shift, unbalance the vessel, and cause it to list.)
Several passengers at the port chose to travel by ship to save on fare and bring more luggage.
“Ang ticket namin for 3 pax nasa 12 [thousand] eh. On the way pa lang,” said Fatima Belarmino, a passenger bound for Cebu.
She added that traveling by airplane would require a budget of P10,000 per person.
Meanwhile, couple Rosanna Layson and Rick Moulton chose to take a ship so they could bring three carts of baggage to Palawan.
“Sa barko madadala namin lahat ng gamit namin sa bahay, durabox, mga chair. Hindi naman namin madadala lahat yan sa airplane,” Layson said.
(On a ship, we can bring all our household items, plastic storage boxes, and chairs. We wouldn't be able to bring all of that on an airplane.)
“Plane is quicker, that’s for sure, but it will be an interesting experience,” Moulton added.
Passenger turnout this year was lower compared to last year, according to the North Port manager. On Friday, passenger volume reached over 1,100.
At the Batangas Port, passenger numbers were also low. From midnight to 4 a.m. on Friday, only over 2,100 passengers arrived, alongside 358 rolling cargoes.
On Thursday, passengers departing from the Batangas pier reached 7,000, compared to 12,000 passengers in 2025.

“Matumal pa ang pagdating ng pasahero ngayon, compared noong isang taon. Nagmahal talaga ang pamasahe. Mauunawaan naman natin ang mga shipping lines because alam naman natin na mataas na ang presyo ng produktong petrolyo,” Batangas Port Manager Aurora Mendoza said.
(Passenger arrivals are still slow today compared to last year. Fares have genuinely increased. We can understand the shipping lines because we know that petroleum product prices are high.)
The PCG reminded the public that shipping companies do not allow the boarding of electric or hybrid vehicles on ships as part of heightened safety precautions. –Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News
